full_judgment: 5. Mr. J. B. M. Hassan, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners submitted that on assessment of evidence of plaintiffs witnesses i.e. P.Ws 1 and 2, the appellate Court came to the conclusion as to exclusive possession of defendant-petitioner effecting the registered deeds of gift. The High Court Division without materials on record treated the same as joint possession traveling beyond the revisional jurisdiction and thereby committed error of law in passing the impugned judgment which warrants interference of this Court; that the defendant's transfer in respect of part of suit land having been admitted by the plaintiffs, compensation for acquisition having been received by the defendant and defendants exclusive possession of the suit land having been admitted by the P.W.2 Mahmudul Huq, the fact of gift has been proved as per requirement of Mohammadan Law having its 3(three) ingredients viz. desire of the donor, delivery of possession and acceptance thereof. In view of such position without finding any inconsistency in the thumb impression of the donor, the High Court Division was wrong in disbelieving the registered instrument merely comparing the hand writing of the scribe inspite of the fact that subsequent documents were written after 8 years and the alive witnesses of the deed deposed supporting the facts of execution of the deeds and as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be interfered with by this Court that the High Court Division acted beyond its revisional jurisdiction interfering with the findings of final Court of fact arrived' at on consideration of materials on record and ignoring the presumption of correctness of the old registered documents and as such, the impugned judgment requires interference by this Court.
